title: His first drum set and the overhead beater
summary: He liked drums best; his first was a tuxedo set with a large bass drum and an overhead beater, which he kept until Chicago.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: Did you like that better than any other instrument I guess? Yeah, I really liked the drums.
I really liked the drums. Yeah.
What was your first set like? Did you get a whole set like?
I had a black tuxedo set. They used to call it a tuxedo. Something like this drum here.
Is it a big bass drum?

Yeah, it was a big bass drum. It was a very big bass drum. You got a big one in the back. I got a big one in the back. Oh yeah, a big 28 inch or something. Yeah, 28. This is a 14 by 22. It was one just like this. It had a single extension on it you see. It didn't have the double. It didn't make the double.
Oh yes, the one head that you could tune that.
It didn't have the old ropes with the...
No. It was the leather. But I did have an overhead beater though.

That overhead trap you know. Yeah. And I had kept that so long until when I went to Chicago. I don't know what happened. I went down. I went to Chicago and I left out of Chicago. I went to Springfield and I missed the place. I never could find it when I got back to Chicago you see. But that's what I had. The old tuxedo drum. Flag drum like that. Then I got a set of Puerl drum. When I went to Chicago. Peacock Puerl. I had about 15 sets I reckon all together. I got about five sets around here now. I always did like a lot of drums. That's nice.
